packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — `createEvent` (and lark/CalDAV equivalents) never accepts the new `credentialId` discriminator added to the `Calendar` interface and still resolves `destinationCalendar[0]`, so in a collective booking every host's credential writes into the first host's externalId — wrong calendar, 404s, or duplicate events for all non-Google providers — confidence 90, P1.

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:267 — `externalId` is echoed into `EventResult` straight from the caller's request rather than from the created event, and is returned even when `creationResult` is undefined, so BookingReference.externalCalendarId records an asserted calendar that may differ from where the provider actually wrote (or where nothing was written at all) — confidence 75, P2.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:339 — the destination loop `await`s `createEvent` serially per host with no timeout, concurrency bound, or partial-failure rollback, so a collective event with N hosts turns one calendar round-trip into N sequential ones and any single slow/failing provider degrades or partially materializes the whole booking — confidence 75, P2.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — `prisma.credential.findUnique` is issued inside the per-destination loop (and again at line 517 inside the per-reference loop) instead of one batched `findMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } } })`, a textbook N+1 on the booking hot path — confidence 100, P2.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:363 — the legacy branch `this.calendarCredentials.filter((c) => c.type === destination.integration)` now runs once per destination inside the outer loop, so M destinations sharing an integration create M×N calendar events and M×N booking references — an O(n^2) duplication cliff that did not exist when destinationCalendar was singular — confidence 75, P1.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063 — when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists the field is `null`, so the very next `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` at line 1078 no-ops and every collective host's destination calendar is silently discarded — the exact case this change exists to fix — confidence 90, P1.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1077 — the assembled `DestinationCalendar[]` has no uniqueness invariant, so an eventType destination that is also a host's destination (or two hosts sharing a calendar) yields duplicate entries and therefore duplicate calendar events and duplicate BookingReferences — confidence 75, P2.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1877 — `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` persists only the first of N calendars, so `Booking.destinationCalendar` becomes redundant derived data that silently means "first host's calendar" and can never be reconciled with the true fan-out recorded in BookingReference — confidence 90, P2.
